verses.pali: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Seated to one side, that mendicant said to the Buddha:

verses.pali: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā valāhakakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī”ti?
verses.english: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why someone, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in the company of the gods of the thundercloud host?”

verses.pali: “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena sucaritaṁ carati, vācāya sucaritaṁ carati, manasā sucaritaṁ carati.
verses.english: “Mendicant, it’s when someone does good things by way of body, speech, and mind.
‘The gods of the thundercloud host are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’

verses.pali: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā valāhakakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.
verses.english: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the gods of the thundercloud host!’

verses.pali: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā valāhakakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
verses.english: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the thundercloud host.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā valāhakakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī”ti.
verses.english: This is the cause, this is the reason why someone, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in the company of the gods of the thundercloud host.”
